The default number of reconnect attempts the Go client makes before it gives up is [10] [2]. To make it retry forever, one would set the `MaxReconnect` option to a negative value, like `-1`.

The Go client library buffers outgoing data so that bigger chunks can be written to the network at one time. [3] When a client buffer's limit is reached, messages will no longer be publishable by the client and an error will be returned. [3]

The Go client ping interval is set to `"2m"` by default [1]. For the Go client, the maximum pings outstanding is set to `2` [1]. Therefore, the Go client pings the server every 2 minutes, and the connection is treated as stale when the client receives no pong in response to more than 2 pings [1].
The max reconnect attempts setting is counted **per server** [2]. When a client has exhausted all servers, it will close the connection and raise an error [4].
[1] Requests made on the `$SRV.STATS.>` subject query statistics from services. Available stats include total requests, total errors, and total processing time.
A pull consumer allows `explicit` acknowledgement mode [5]. There is no mode that acknowledges a whole batch at once in pull consumers [5].

[1] After you revoke a user with nsc, you need to 'push' the revocations to the servers for the changes to take effect. Specifically, you would use `nsc push -i` or `nsc push -a B -u nats://localhost`. [1]

The consumer worker should send a `term()` message to keep the message from being redelivered [5]. The payload on the wire is indicated by the type of acknowledgment being sent, which in this case is `term()`.

The default delay between reconnect attempts in the Go client is 2 seconds [3]. This setting is not only enforced between attempts to any server, but it is also applicable to attempts to the same server [3].
